why: Route pages call it a low-angle snowfield that turns to ice late in the season, but one trip report saw open crevasses in the fall, so the sources disagree.
The line is reached by climbing Andrews Glacier, which the pages describe inconsistently (plain snow slope versus reported fall crevasses); no page describes this couloir's own crossing.
Only a thin area listing as a snow couloir near Andrews Glacier turned up, with nothing on glacier travel.

Held at unsure on review: the line crosses the Isabelle Glacier, and the no rests only on no crevasses being named. The route page and a trip report describe a steep snow ramp off a small cirque glacier, climbed with axe and crampons and descended by glissading, with no rope used and no crevasses named.

The climbing page places it on a rock wall in the Sangre de Cristo with only early-season snow in the descent slot and no glacier mentioned; whether the base snowfield lasts through the season stayed unclear.
A rock route whose fastest descent uses Andrews Glacier (disputed crevasse status), with a snow gully as the alternative.
A club page calls Mary's Glacier a semi-permanent snowfield rather than a glacier, and the route page describes a snow couloir with optional pickets and no crevasses.
The route page describes a snow couloir where snow pulls away from the rock in places, and a solo trip report treats it as snow slopes with avalanche concern and no glacier.
Listings describe a snow and ice couloir reached from the Solitude side with Andrews Glacier only an optional descent, but no page read described the line's own hazards.
The route page describes a long couloir on the west side of the Divide with a short ice step and ice axes in use, and the snowfield is only an alternative descent.
The route page describes a short spring mixed climb on the north face with steep snow, and mentions Tyndall Glacier only as a descent option.
The route page describes a snow couloir largely separated from Tyndall Glacier by a rock rib, soloed with optional pickets, soft snow in July and ice later.
Route pages place it on Flattop's south face with winter and spring ascents, steep snow and mixed pitches, and no glacier.
A short rock route whose escape walks down Andrews Glacier, which the pages describe inconsistently.

Held at unsure on review: the line crosses the Mills Glacier and no page rules out crevasses there. A rappel line off Broadway that ends at Mills Glacier, which the park's research page does not count as a flowing glacier, and no climbing page gives crevasses for it.
The area page places it in the Pikes Peak cirque, a winter and spring mixed and snow area with no glacier mentioned.
The area page places it in French Creek on Pikes Peak, a winter and spring mixed objective with a moderate to steep snow approach and no glacier.

Held at unsure on review: the line crosses the Mills Glacier and no page rules out crevasses there. Route pages approach via Chasm Lake and Lamb's Slide and describe a heavy-sluff snow couloir, and the park research page does not count Mills as a flowing glacier.

Held at unsure on review: the line crosses the Mills Glacier and no page rules out crevasses there. The approach page has parties hiking past Chasm Lake and climbing snow over Mills Glacier toward a snow tongue, with no crevasses described.
